grade.first_issue: The necessity argument first fails when the displayed bounds on ε(y+c) are asserted without derivation; this is the central step meant to restrict an arbitrary function, so Rule E applies.
grade.summary: The claimed classification is correct, and the submission correctly verifies every translation f(x)=x+c with c≥0. However, it does not prove that these are the only solutions. The asserted ε-recurrence is unsupported, and even that recurrence would not imply the claimed convergence: when c=0, its two inequalities are tautological and impose no convergence at all. Moreover, asymptotic convergence of ε would not establish that ε is constant on the whole domain. Repairing the proof requires the missing central rigidity argument, not a local correction.
strengths: Correctly verifies the right inequality for f(x)=x+c using AM-GM.
Correctly verifies the left inequality for f(x)=x+c using RMS-AM.
Correctly determines that the only solutions within the restricted family f(x)=ax are obtained when a=1.

errors.description: The displayed bounds involving ε(y+c) are introduced merely by saying they were found through growth analysis; no derivation from the original inequalities is supplied.
The inference that those bounds force ε(y) to converge is invalid. In particular, for c=0 the bounds reduce to inequalities that hold identically for arbitrary ε.
Even convergence of ε at infinity would not imply that ε is constant for all positive inputs, so it would not complete the required uniqueness proof.
The choice x=y+c is not justified for all y because c=f(1)-1 has not yet been shown nonnegative; it is only automatically admissible for sufficiently large y.
